$comment: Branch protection for this repository, in the exact request shape of
PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches/{branch}/protection (#162).
Every field here follows ADR-095's protection table, which is the accepted
decision and the source of truth. An earlier draft of this file diverged from
it in four places without saying so — the review caught all four. A governance
artifact that quietly contradicts the governing ADR is worse than none, because
it looks authoritative.
Settings that live only in the GitHub UI are settings nobody can review, diff,
or restore. This file is the reviewable copy; scripts/check-branch-protection.py
checks it against docs/ci/REQUIRED-CHECKS.md on every PR, and against the live
API when given a token.
Not self-applying. Applying it needs admin scope:
scripts/check-branch-protection.py --apply develop   (prints the call)
Checks whose scope the contract can see is base-coupled, but whose target
branch it cannot read — a job `if:` narrows on a GitHub expression, and
evaluating that language is out of scope for the contract generator.
Declared rather than guessed, for the same reason the advisory map is:
a check that is silently assumed main-only can be required on a branch
where it never reports, and branch protection then waits on `Expected`
forever. If a check gains a base_ref condition and is not listed here,
the audit refuses to let any branch require it.
ADR-095: PR-gated, 0 required approvals, linear history, no force-push,
no deletion. The 15 checks that run on every PR regardless of base.
CodeQL and the container scan are absent because they do not run on a
develop-based PR at all — requiring a check that never reports leaves
the PR waiting on an `Expected` status forever.
ADR-095's stabilization tier: develop -> integration -> main. Same
protection as develop, and the same 15 checks for the same reason.
Omitting it left the promotion path open — a change could reach
integration directly, or red, and then be promoted to main through a
gate that only ever inspected the integration->main hop.
ADR-095: 1 required approval on the release tier, and only here.
CI cannot tell whether a test proves its criterion or merely restates
it, and a tautological test passes every gate in the chain.
Nineteen checks: the fifteen above plus the four that only run on a
main-based PR — CodeQL's three matrix legs, and the container scan
whose job `if:` tests base_ref == 'main'. On main they report, so on
main they are required.
enforce_admins stays false here, per ADR-095: 'a solo maintainer/agent
isn't deadlocked'. It is also load-bearing for the cage guard, whose
own failure message says an admin may merge a legitimate cage/eval
change manually — true only while admins can bypass a required check.
Checks that run on PRs and are deliberately NOT required, each with the
reason. check-branch-protection.py fails when a PR check is in neither
this map nor a branch's contexts — so adding a gate to CI forces a
decision about whether it is part of the merge contract, rather than
letting it default to advisory by being forgotten.
Auto-merge is safe only once the contexts above are required: GitHub's
auto-merge waits for *required* checks, so arming it with none configured
merges immediately. That ordering is the whole reason #162 is blocked by
#161 — the names have to exist and be stable first.
Linear history is required on all three branches (ADR-095), so merges are
squash or rebase, never merge commits.
